module.title: Unit 10: Environmental Jurisprudence & Climate Legislation
module.objective: Mampu membahas traktat iklim internasional dan kepatuhan hukum lingkungan menggunakan register hukum formal.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Climate Treaties and Legal Duties
subModules.grammarFocus: Formal legal obligations, passive voice with nominalisation, and conditional clauses
subModules.vocabularyFocus: International climate treaties, legal compliance, enforcement, and liability

content.summary: Read a short report about how climate treaties create duties for governments and how those duties may be monitored. You will identify the main argument, find legal details, and notice formal grammar often used in legislation and treaty documents.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Practise shall and must for legal duties, passive structures with nouns such as ratification and enforcement, and conditional clauses that describe the results of non-compliance.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Learn terms for treaties, legal authority, duties, environmental damage, and action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the passage to find its main point. Then scan for names, dates, legal duties, and consequences. Use nearby words to check the meaning of unfamiliar legal terms.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short B2 text about climate treaties and national legal duties.
Locate details about ratification, reporting, compliance, and possible consequences.
Recognize how shall and must express legal obligations.
Identify passive voice and nominalisation in formal legal writing.
Use conditional clauses to understand what may happen after a breach of a legal duty.

contextWarmup.prompt: A country signs a climate treaty but does not meet its agreed emissions target. What is the most useful first step for assessing the situation?
options: Check the treaty's duties and the country's reported progress.
Assume that signing the treaty means the target has been met.
Decide that an international court can automatically punish the country.
contextWarmup.explanation: A careful assessment starts with the treaty text and evidence of progress. Signing or ratifying an agreement does not prove compliance, and a court's power depends on its jurisdiction and the relevant legal rules.

rules: In formal legal writing, shall often introduces a duty: Each party shall submit a progress report.
Must also expresses a strong requirement and is common in regulations and clear legal guidance.
Passive voice and nominalisation can focus attention on a legal process rather than on the person carrying it out: The report must be submitted.
A conditional clause can connect a failure to comply with a consequence: Where a party fails to report, further review shall be required.

commonTrap.explanation: Do not treat signing, ratifying, and complying as the same action. Ratification is a formal approval of an agreement, while compliance concerns whether a party follows its duties.
commonTrap.wrong: The country ratified the treaty, so it must have met every emissions target.
commonTrap.correct: The country ratified the treaty, but its compliance with each emissions target must be assessed separately.

content.passageTitle: From Climate Promise to Legal Duty
paragraphs: When a government ratifies an international climate treaty, it formally accepts the agreement, but ratification alone does not cut emissions. The treaty may require each party to publish a national plan, set targets, and report its progress. These duties give other governments and the public information with which to assess compliance. The exact obligations depend on the wording of the agreement and the laws of each country.

A review body can examine reports, ask for further information, and identify areas where a party has fallen behind. Its role is not always the same as that of a court. A court may consider a dispute only when it has jurisdiction, which can depend on the consent of the states involved and the terms of the relevant treaty. For this reason, international climate rules do not create one automatic legal process for every disagreement.

Domestic legislation can make treaty goals more practical. A national law may require public agencies to measure emissions, prepare reduction plans, and explain delays. In formal legal writing, a duty may be expressed with shall: Each agency shall submit an annual report. Passive structures can also emphasise the required action: The report shall be submitted by 30 June. Such wording highlights the duty, even when the responsible official is not named.

Consequences for a breach vary between agreements and legal systems. Where a party fails to meet a reporting duty, the treaty may provide for review, requests for correction, or other steps. It does not follow that every missed target leads to a fine or a court case. Liability for environmental harm may also require evidence about the cause of the damage and the applicable law. Clear enforcement rules, reliable information, and fair review can help make climate commitments meaningful.

drills.instruction: Match each term to its meaning in the passage.

pairs.right: Following the duties or rules that apply
A court's legal authority to hear a dispute
Legal responsibility for harm or a breach
Steps taken to make rules effective
Action intended to reduce emissions or climate risks

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Ratifying a treaty is only one part of turning climate promises into duties that can be reviewed.
Every climate treaty gives courts the same power to punish governments.
National laws have replaced all international climate agreements.
questions.answer: Ratifying a treaty is only one part of turning climate promises into duties that can be reviewed.
questions.explanation: The passage explains that ratification does not itself cut emissions. Reporting, national laws, review, and enforcement also matter.

questions.question: According to the first paragraph, what may a treaty require each party to do?
options: Publish a national plan, set targets, and report progress.
Give every court power over all climate disputes.
Pay a fine as soon as it ratifies the agreement.
questions.answer: Publish a national plan, set targets, and report progress.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says a treaty may require parties to publish plans, set targets, and report progress.

questions.question: Why does a court's jurisdiction matter in an international climate dispute?
options: It determines whether the court has legal authority to consider the dispute.
It proves that the state has already met its emissions target.
It decides how a country must write its national plan.
questions.answer: It determines whether the court has legal authority to consider the dispute.
questions.explanation: The passage says a court may consider a dispute only when it has jurisdiction, which can depend on state consent and treaty terms.

questions.question: What can a review body do, according to the passage?
options: Examine reports and request further information.
Automatically impose a fine for every missed target.
Replace national agencies responsible for measuring emissions.
questions.answer: Examine reports and request further information.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph states that a review body can examine reports, ask for information, and identify areas where a party has fallen behind.

questions.question: What does the word 'compliance' refer to in the first paragraph?
options: Whether a party follows its treaty duties.
Whether a court accepts the consent of a state.
Whether an agency publishes a law in a newspaper.
questions.answer: Whether a party follows its treaty duties.
questions.explanation: The passage says that reports provide information with which governments and the public can assess compliance with treaty duties.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'shall' in the sentence 'Each agency shall submit an annual report'?
options: It expresses a formal duty.
It describes an action that happened in the past.
It suggests that submitting a report is optional.
questions.explanation: The passage gives this sentence as an example of how shall expresses a duty in formal legal writing.

questions.question: Why might a legal text say, 'The report shall be submitted by 30 June'?
options: The passive structure emphasises the required action and deadline.
The sentence identifies the official who wrote the report.
The sentence shows that the report has already been submitted.
questions.answer: The passive structure emphasises the required action and deadline.
questions.explanation: The passage explains that passive structures can emphasise the action required, even when the responsible official is not named.

questions.question: What may happen if a party fails to meet a reporting duty?
options: The treaty may provide for review or requests for correction.
The party must always be fined by an international court.
The treaty automatically loses legal force.
questions.answer: The treaty may provide for review or requests for correction.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph lists review and requests for correction as possible steps, while warning that consequences vary.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a missed emissions target?
options: It does not always lead to a fine or court case.
It always proves that the state has caused environmental harm.
It immediately gives every review body court powers.
questions.answer: It does not always lead to a fine or court case.
questions.explanation: The passage states that it does not follow that every missed target leads to a fine or a court case.

questions.question: What may be needed to establish liability for environmental harm?
options: Evidence about the cause of the damage and the applicable law.
Proof that the country has signed any international agreement.
A report showing that every party met its targets.
questions.answer: Evidence about the cause of the damage and the applicable law.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph says liability may require evidence about the cause of the damage and the law that applies.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Debating Climate Treaties and Legal Enforcement

content.summary: This briefing prepares you to follow a fast, informal academic conversation between two law students discussing climate agreements. You will focus on identifying legal concepts, tracking contrasting viewpoints, and recognizing consonant-to-vowel linking in rapid speech.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a spoken conversation about international environmental treaties.
Identify details such as treaty clauses, enforcement mechanisms, and student proposals.
Notice how words link together in connected speech when consonant sounds meet vowel sounds.

keyPhrases.note: Used in legal contexts to describe procedures that ensure states adhere to treaty obligations.
Formal penalties imposed on parties that violate international laws or agreements.
Close and critical observation of actions by citizens, journalists, and global organizations.
Formal secondary agreements added to an existing treaty to strengthen specific obligations.

connectedSpeech.note: The voiced alveolar fricative /z/ links smoothly to the short open vowel /ɒ/.
The final voiceless stop /t/ attaches directly to the weak schwa /ə/ of away.
In standard British pronunciation, linking /r/ surfaces between the schwa and the vowel /ɒ/.
The final stop consonant /t/ shifts forward to begin the syllable with the short vowel /ɪ/.

sections.title: Audio Dialogue: Preparing the Environmental Law Seminar

content.context: Two law students, Alex and Morgan, are sitting in the campus library discussing their upcoming presentation on the Paris Agreement and international environmental law.
content.audioPrompt: Listen to the conversation between two friends preparing their seminar presentation.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Have you checked the Paris Agreement notes?
lines.translation: Sudahkah kamu memeriksa catatan Perjanjian Paris?

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: Yes, the compliance system looks pretty weak.
lines.translation: Ya, sistem kepatuhannya terlihat cukup lemah.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: It relies on voluntary emission targets.
lines.translation: Itu bergantung pada target emisi sukarela.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: That makes legal enforcement really tough.
lines.translation: Itu membuat penegakan hukum menjadi sangat sulit.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Kyoto had binding reduction targets instead.
lines.translation: Sebaliknya, Kyoto memiliki target pengurangan yang mengikat.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: True, but countries just walked away.
lines.translation: Benar, tapi negara-negara malah menarik diri.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: There are no punitive sanctions now.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: Article thirteen still demands clear reports.
lines.translation: Pasal tiga belas masih menuntut laporan yang jelas.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Does public scrutiny create real accountability?
lines.translation: Apakah pengawasan publik menciptakan akuntabilitas nyata?

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: It puts pressure on major polluters.
lines.translation: Itu memberi tekanan pada para pencemar utama.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: We need binding supplementary protocols soon.
lines.translation: Kita butuh protokol tambahan yang mengikat segera.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: Let's argue that in our seminar.
lines.translation: Mari kita kemukakan itu dalam seminar kita.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Drafting Formal Climate Legislation and Legal Clauses

content.summary: This writing guide covers formal legislative registers used in international climate treaties and environmental law. You will learn to draft binding obligations with statutory modals, apply nominalisation for impersonal authority, and structure precise conditional clauses detailing legal breach and liability.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Drafting Binding Obligations (Statutory Modals)
blueprintItems.formula: Subject (Signatory/Party) + shall / must + base verb + Object / Complement
blueprintItems.example: Each signatory state shall reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by forty percent before 2030.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Nominalisation with Passive Construction
blueprintItems.formula: Nominalised Action Phrase + Passive Verb + Prepositional Agent / Standard
blueprintItems.example: The ratification of the climate accord was completed by all participating states.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Structuring Statutory Breach and Liability Clauses
blueprintItems.formula: Where / If + Subject + fails to comply with / is in breach of + Legal Instrument, Subject + shall be liable to + Sanction
blueprintItems.example: Where a contracting party fails to comply with emission ceilings, that party shall be liable to financial penalties under the treaty framework.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize formal names of treaties, legislation, and defined statutory parties.
mechanicsRules.badExample: the member states ratified the paris agreement during the summit.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The member states ratified the Paris Agreement during the summit.
mechanicsRules.why: Official titles of treaties, legal acts, and specific defined entities represent proper nouns in legal English.

mechanicsRules.rule: Distinguish strictly between 'shall' and 'should' in statutory drafting.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Each commercial operator should submit an emission report annually.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Each commercial operator shall submit an emission report annually.
mechanicsRules.why: In legal registers, 'shall' creates an enforceable legal duty, whereas 'should' merely suggests a non-binding recommendation.

mechanicsRules.rule: Set off introductory statutory conditions with a comma.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Where an industrial facility discharges untreated water it shall be liable to immediate prosecution.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Where an industrial facility discharges untreated water, it shall be liable to immediate prosecution.
mechanicsRules.why: Dependent clauses beginning with conditional words like 'where' or 'if' must be followed by a comma to keep the legal trigger distinct from the resulting liability.

sampleSentences.en: All signatory states shall submit a verified decarbonisation report on an annual basis.
sampleSentences.id: Semua negara penandatangan wajib menyerahkan laporan dekarbonisasi yang terverifikasi setiap tahun.

sampleSentences.en: The enforcement of stricter conservation measures was mandated by the environmental tribunal.
sampleSentences.id: Penerapan tindakan konservasi yang lebih ketat dimandatkan oleh pengadilan lingkungan hidup.

sampleSentences.en: Where an operator fails to comply with statutory waste standards, it shall be liable to immediate fines.
sampleSentences.id: Apabila operator gagal mematuhi standar limbah menurut undang-undang, operator tersebut akan dikenai denda langsung.

sampleSentences.en: The imposition of legal sanctions will take place if an enterprise is in breach of ecological accords.
sampleSentences.id: Pemberlakuan sanksi hukum akan dilakukan jika suatu perusahaan melanggar kesepakatan ekologis.
sampleSentences.focus: Nominalised subject with conditional breach clause

mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Where a corporation violates the Clean Air Act, it will be liable to administrative penalties.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Apabila sebuah korporasi melanggar Undang-Undang Udara Bersih, korporasi tersebut akan dikenai hukuman administratif.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Capitalize the initial word and the statutory title, and place a comma after the introductory conditional clause.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Drafting a Treaty Obligation Clause
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three formal sentences outlining legal obligations for industrial operators under a regional environmental directive. Use 'shall' for mandatory actions and include at least one passive nominalised phrase (such as 'The reduction of pollutants is required').
guidedLabChallenges.example: Industrial operators shall reduce their water usage by twenty percent within twelve months. The installation of sustainable filtration systems is required for all production plants. Each facility shall submit an independently verified sustainability audit twice per year.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Draft your formal legislative obligations here...

guidedLabChallenges.title: Drafting a Breach and Liability Notice
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Draft a formal statutory compliance notice of three to four sentences. Use the conditional pattern 'Where/If + Subject + fails to comply / is in breach of..., Subject + shall be liable to...' and specify concrete legal consequences.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Where a commercial entity fails to comply with statutory carbon limits, that entity shall be liable to immediate financial sanctions. If an operator is in breach of environmental preservation orders, its operational license shall be revoked. Corrective action must be demonstrated within thirty calendar days.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Draft your breach and consequence clauses here...

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the active sentence into a formal legal passive sentence using the nominalised noun phrase 'The enforcement of':
practicumQuestions.promptText: The international tribunal enforced the ecological protection decree.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin with 'The enforcement of the ecological protection decree was...'
targetAnswers: The enforcement of the ecological protection decree was carried out by the international tribunal.
The enforcement of the ecological protection decree was undertaken by the international tribunal.
The enforcement of the ecological protection decree was conducted by the international tribunal.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Transforming the verb 'enforced' into the nominalisation 'enforcement' and employing a passive structure produces an impersonal, formal legal tone.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform this informal sentence into a formal statutory obligation using the modal verb 'shall':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Every member state needs to cut carbon emissions by thirty percent.
practicumQuestions.hint: Replace 'needs to cut' with 'shall reduce' or 'shall cut'.
targetAnswers: Every member state shall reduce carbon emissions by thirty percent.
Every member state shall cut carbon emissions by thirty percent.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In formal legislative drafting, 'shall' establishes an enforceable legal obligation rather than a simple necessity or recommendation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences into a single statutory condition starting with the word 'Where':
practicumQuestions.promptText: A company fails to comply with the waste management protocol. It shall be liable to statutory fines.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'Where a company fails to comply...' and add a comma before the main clause.
targetAnswers: Where a company fails to comply with the waste management protocol, it shall be liable to statutory fines.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Formal legislative texts commonly use 'Where' to introduce conditional circumstances of non-compliance, separated from the sanction by a comma.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the capitalization and punctuation errors in this legal statement:
practicumQuestions.promptText: according to the kyoto protocol industrialized nations must report their emissions annually
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word and the proper name of the treaty, and insert appropriate commas and a full stop.
targetAnswers: According to the Kyoto Protocol, industrialized nations must report their emissions annually.
According to the Kyoto Protocol, industrialised nations must report their emissions annually.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Kyoto Protocol' is a proper noun naming a specific treaty, the opening prepositional phrase requires a comma, and the sentence requires an initial capital and closing period.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the following sentence using the nominalisation 'The approval of...':
practicumQuestions.promptText: The ministry approved the sustainable energy initiative.
practicumQuestions.hint: Convert 'approved' to 'approval' and use a passive construction such as 'was granted' or 'was completed'.
targetAnswers: The approval of the sustainable energy initiative was granted by the ministry.
The approval of the sustainable energy initiative was completed by the ministry.
The approval of the sustainable energy initiative was finalized by the ministry.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Nominalising the action as 'The approval of...' shifts the focus from the ministry to the administrative process itself.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using the phrase 'is in breach of' to form a conditional legal statement beginning with 'If':
practicumQuestions.promptText: A corporation violates the international treaty. It shall face economic sanctions.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'If a corporation is in breach of...' followed by a comma.
targetAnswers: If a corporation is in breach of the international treaty, it shall face economic sanctions.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The phrase 'is in breach of' is standard legal terminology for non-compliance with a formal agreement or statute.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct all capitalization and punctuation errors in this statutory clause:
practicumQuestions.promptText: each signatory state shall preserve biological diversity under the paris agreement
practicumQuestions.hint: Ensure the first letter and treaty name are capitalized, and add terminal punctuation.
targetAnswers: Each signatory state shall preserve biological diversity under the Paris Agreement.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The sentence must open with a capital letter, 'Paris Agreement' must be capitalized as a formal legal instrument, and a period must close the sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence into formal passive legal register starting with 'The implementation of':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Authorities must implement the conservation scheme immediately.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'The implementation of the conservation scheme must be carried out...' or 'must be undertaken...'
targetAnswers: The implementation of the conservation scheme must be carried out immediately.
The implementation of the conservation scheme must be undertaken immediately.
The implementation of the conservation scheme is required immediately.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Converting 'must implement' into 'The implementation of... must be carried out' creates the impersonal tone required in statutory texts.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the statutory sentence by placing the verb phrase into the correct present tense form for non-compliance:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Where an enterprise ________ (fail to comply) with environmental standards, it shall be liable to prosecution.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use third-person singular present: 'fails to comply'.
targetAnswers: Where an enterprise fails to comply with environmental standards, it shall be liable to prosecution.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Statutory conditional clauses referring to general application use the simple present tense ('fails to comply') for the third-person singular subject.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Draft a single formal legal obligation sentence starting with 'Municipal councils shall' stating that they must audit water quality twice a year:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Write a complete statutory obligation for municipal councils to inspect or audit local water quality twice per year.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin with 'Municipal councils shall audit...' and specify the frequency.
targetAnswers: Municipal councils shall audit local water quality twice a year.
Municipal councils shall audit local water quality twice per year.
Municipal councils shall audit water quality twice a year.
Municipal councils shall audit water quality twice per year.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The sentence directly applies the formula 'Subject + shall + base verb + Object + time complement' to create a binding statutory rule.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Climate Treaties and Legal Compliance

content.summary: Practise discussing climate treaties, legal obligations, and environmental compliance in a clear, formal register. Support your points with reasons, distinguish legal authority from political influence, and use precise terms such as ratification, jurisdiction, liability, enforcement, and mitigation.
content.audioGuidance: Speak at a measured pace and make each key legal term clear. Stress the main content words, pause briefly between claims and supporting reasons, and use falling intonation to finish statements. Use rising intonation for genuine yes-or-no questions, not for every sentence.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Distinguish short and long vowel sounds
pillars.explanation: Keep vowel sounds distinct in words such as treaty, legal, and climate. Avoid shortening stressed vowels so much that a listener has difficulty recognising the word.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.target: Stress the correct syllable in formal vocabulary
pillars.explanation: Practise the stress in ratification, compliance, jurisdiction, liability, enforcement, and mitigation. Say each word slowly first, then use it in a complete sentence.

pillars.name: Formal Register
pillars.target: Use precise language and complete clauses
pillars.explanation: Prefer phrases such as the state is legally bound to comply and the court may have jurisdiction. Avoid overly casual expressions when discussing legal duties.

pillars.name: Sentence Intonation
pillars.explanation: Use a steady falling tone for conclusions. Raise your tone slightly when asking a direct question, and stress contrast words such as however and whereas.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Ratification is stressed on CA, while compliance is stressed on PLI. Keep the stressed syllable clear in both words.
Jurisdiction is stressed on DIC and liability on BIL. Give the stressed syllable more prominence without making the other syllables disappear.
The main stress falls on FORCE in enforcement and GA in mitigation. Practise each word before using it in a sentence.
Obligation is stressed on GA, while environmental is stressed on VI. Keep the rhythm natural rather than stressing every syllable.

drills.targetText: The ratification of the climate treaty creates a legal obligation for each party.
drills.phonetic: /ðə ˌrætɪfɪˈkeɪʃən əv ðə ˈklaɪmət ˈtriːti kriˈeɪts ə ˈliːɡəl ˌɒblɪˈɡeɪʃən fə iːtʃ ˈpɑːti/
drills.focus: Stress in ratification, treaty, and obligation
drills.hint: Say the sentence in two thought groups, pausing briefly after treaty.

drills.targetText: The tribunal questioned the state's compliance with its emission targets.
drills.phonetic: /ðə traɪˈbjuːnəl ˈkwestʃənd ðə steɪts kəmˈplaɪəns wɪð ɪts ɪˈmɪʃən ˈtɑːɡɪts/
drills.focus: Clear stress in tribunal, compliance, and emission
drills.hint: Make the main stress in compliance easy to hear, then link with its smoothly.

drills.targetText: The court's jurisdiction depends on the terms of the agreement.
drills.phonetic: /ðə kɔːts ˌdʒʊərɪsˈdɪkʃən dɪˈpendz ɒn ðə tɜːmz əv ði əˈɡriːmənt/
drills.hint: Do not rush jurisdiction. Place the strongest stress on DIC.

drills.targetText: Effective enforcement can reduce liability and support climate mitigation.
drills.phonetic: /ɪˈfektɪv ɪnˈfɔːsmənt kən rɪˈdjuːs ˌlaɪəˈbɪləti ən səˈpɔːt ˈklaɪmət ˌmɪtɪˈɡeɪʃən/
drills.focus: Natural rhythm across a formal statement
drills.hint: Stress effective, enforcement, liability, and mitigation. Keep can and and short.

roleplay.context: You are taking part in a public consultation about a proposed national climate law. A legal adviser asks how international treaty commitments should be reflected in domestic legislation.

turns.speaker: Legal Adviser
turns.text: Has your government ratified the climate treaty, and what domestic obligations follow?
turns.translation: Apakah pemerintah Anda telah meratifikasi traktat iklim tersebut, dan kewajiban domestik apa yang mengikutinya?

turns.speaker: Policy Delegate
turns.text: Yes. Ratification commits the state to report its progress and pursue its mitigation targets.
turns.translation: Ya. Ratifikasi mewajibkan negara untuk melaporkan kemajuannya dan mengupayakan target mitigasinya.

turns.speaker: Legal Adviser
turns.text: Which institution should assess compliance, and does it have the necessary jurisdiction?
turns.translation: Lembaga mana yang seharusnya menilai kepatuhan, dan apakah lembaga itu memiliki yurisdiksi yang diperlukan?

turns.speaker: Policy Delegate
turns.text: An independent regulator should assess compliance. Parliament must also give it clear enforcement powers.
turns.translation: Regulator independen seharusnya menilai kepatuhan. Parlemen juga harus memberinya kewenangan penegakan yang jelas.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds. Tell a clear story about a fictional dispute over a company's pollution, and explain how the case was handled.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe an environmental dispute from the first complaint to the final legal decision.
storyPoints: Explain what environmental harm was reported and who raised the complaint.
Describe which authority or court considered the case and why it had jurisdiction.
Say whether the company faced liability and what enforcement or remediation followed.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The court found the company liable for the damage and ordered it to fund environmental remediation.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə kɔːt faʊnd ðə ˈkʌmpəni ˈlaɪəbəl fə ðə ˈdæmɪdʒ ən ˈɔːdəd ɪt tə fʌnd ɪnˌvaɪrənˈmentəl ˌriːəˌmɪdiˈeɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Organise the account in chronological order and use formal legal vocabulary accurately.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds. Explain how a fictional country moved from ratifying a climate treaty to implementing its commitments.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell the story of a country putting its climate treaty commitments into practice.
storyPoints: Describe the decision to ratify the treaty and the reasons for it.
Explain how the government introduced domestic mitigation measures and reporting rules.
Describe how compliance was reviewed and what happened when a target was missed.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: After ratification, the government introduced mitigation rules and established a system to review compliance.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈɑːftə ˌrætɪfɪˈkeɪʃən ðə ˈɡʌvənmənt ˌɪntrəˈdjuːst ˌmɪtɪˈɡeɪʃən ruːlz ən ɪˈstæblɪʃt ə ˈsɪstəm tə rɪˈvjuː kəmˈplaɪəns/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use past-tense verbs to show the sequence of events, and explain the link between treaty commitments and national law.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay. Answer the adviser, explain your position, and give at least one reason.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A legal adviser asks whether your country should ratify a new climate treaty.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A parliamentary committee is considering a new climate treaty. Members want to understand what ratification would require and how the government would report progress.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a policy delegate. Explain whether you support ratification, name one obligation it would create, and respond to the adviser's questions in a formal register.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I support ratification, provided that the treaty's reporting duties are matched by a clear domestic implementation plan.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ səˈpɔːt ˌrætɪfɪˈkeɪʃən prəˈvaɪdɪd ðət ðə ˈtriːtiz rɪˈpɔːtɪŋ ˈdjuːtiz ə mætʃt baɪ ə klɪə dəˈmestɪk ˌɪmplɪmenˈteɪʃən plæn/
practicumQuestions.explanation: State your position directly and use a condition or reason to make your response more precise.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay. Explain how compliance should be assessed and what evidence is needed.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: An auditor asks how the government can demonstrate compliance with its emission targets.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: An independent auditor is reviewing a national climate programme and has requested evidence that emission targets are being met.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a government legal officer. Describe the records, reporting procedures, and review process used to demonstrate compliance.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: We can demonstrate compliance through verified emissions data, annual reports, and independent review.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /wi kən ˈdemənstreɪt kəmˈplaɪəns θruː ˈverɪfaɪd ɪˈmɪʃənz ˈdeɪtə ˈænjuəl rɪˈpɔːts ən ˌɪndɪˈpendənt rɪˈvjuː/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Give specific forms of evidence and explain who checks them.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay. Discuss which body should hear the dispute and explain the limits of its authority.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A colleague asks whether an international court can hear a dispute between two states about a climate treaty.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Two states disagree about the interpretation of an environmental treaty. Your team is preparing advice on whether an international court can hear the case.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a legal adviser. Explain that jurisdiction depends on the court's authority and the states' consent under the applicable rules.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The court may have jurisdiction if the treaty and the states' consent allow it to hear this dispute.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə kɔːt meɪ hæv ˌdʒʊərɪsˈdɪkʃən ɪf ðə ˈtriːti ən ðə steɪts kənˈsent əˈlaʊ ɪt tə hɪə ðɪs dɪˈspjuːt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Avoid claiming that a court can always hear the case. Use conditional language to show the limits of jurisdiction.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay. Present your view on liability and propose a fair enforcement response.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A hearing chair asks who should pay for damage caused by a factory that exceeded its legal emission limit.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: At a regulatory hearing, evidence suggests that a factory exceeded its legal emission limit and caused local environmental damage.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You represent a residents' association. Explain why the company may be liable and recommend proportionate enforcement and remediation.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If the evidence confirms the breach, the company should be held liable and required to fund remediation.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf ði ˈevɪdəns kənˈfɜːmz ðə briːtʃ ðə ˈkʌmpəni ʃəd bi held ˈlaɪəbəl ən rɪˈkwaɪəd tə fʌnd ˌriːəˌmɪdiˈeɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Connect the proposed legal consequence to the evidence, and distinguish liability from the practical remedy.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds. Define ratification, compliance, and mitigation, then use each word in a sentence about climate law.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Explain the difference between ratification, compliance, and mitigation in the context of an international climate treaty.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Ratification approves a treaty, compliance concerns following its rules, and mitigation means reducing climate risks or emissions.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˌrætɪfɪˈkeɪʃən əˈpruːvz ə ˈtriːti kəmˈplaɪəns kənˈsɜːnz ˈfɒləʊɪŋ ɪts ruːlz ən ˌmɪtɪˈɡeɪʃən miːnz rɪˈdjuːsɪŋ ˈklaɪmət rɪsks ɔːr ɪˈmɪʃənz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Show that you understand the different meanings by defining each term and using it accurately.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the idea aloud using a formal conditional sentence. Give a realistic consequence of failing to comply with a climate law.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Explain what may happen if a company fails to comply with an emissions regulation.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If a company fails to comply with the regulation, the authority may impose a penalty and require corrective action.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf ə ˈkʌmpəni feɪlz tə kəmˈplaɪ wɪð ðə ˌreɡjʊˈleɪʃən ði ɔːˈθɒrəti meɪ ɪmˈpəʊz ə ˈpenəlti ən rɪˈkwaɪə kəˈrektɪv ˈækʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use the present simple in the if-clause and a modal verb such as may or must in the main clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the sentence three times. Make the stressed syllables in jurisdiction, enforcement, and mitigation clear.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practise the key word stress in this formal statement.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The court's jurisdiction supports enforcement of the mitigation rules.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə kɔːts ˌdʒʊərɪsˈdɪkʃən səˈpɔːts ɪnˈfɔːsmənt əv ðə ˌmɪtɪˈɡeɪʃən ruːlz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Stress DIC in jurisdiction, FORCE in enforcement, and GA in mitigation. Keep the unstressed syllables short but audible.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the first sentence with rising intonation as a genuine yes-or-no question. Say the second with falling intonation as a conclusion.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Use question intonation to check a legal point, then use a falling tone to give your conclusion.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Has the state ratified the treaty? The reporting obligation is now in force.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /hæz ðə steɪt ˈrætɪfaɪd ðə ˈtriːti | ðə rɪˈpɔːtɪŋ ˌɒblɪˈɡeɪʃən ɪz naʊ ɪn fɔːs/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice rise slightly at the end of the direct question, then fall clearly at the end of the statement.
